questions.question: Two forces of equal size, acting in opposite directions on an object, are described as what?
options: Balanced
Unbalanced
Resultant
Frictional

questions.question: How do we find the resultant force acting on an object when multiple forces are present?
options: By multiplying the two largest forces together
By taking the sum of the forces, accounting for their directions
By dividing the total force by the mass of the object
By only measuring the force acting in the direction of gravity

questions.question: If two unequal forces act in opposite directions on an object, which way does the resultant force act?
options: In the direction of the smaller force
In the direction of the bigger force
At a right angle to both forces
In the direction of the earth's gravity

questions.question: What is the effect of applying a greater resultant force on a given object?
options: The object will experience a smaller or slower change in speed.
The object will experience a greater or faster change in speed.
The object's mass will immediately increase.
The object will completely stop experiencing any frictional forces.

questions.question: What is friction?
options: The force of one surface gripping or rubbing on another.
The pull of gravity acting on a heavy object.
The upward push of a liquid on a floating object.
The magnetic attraction between two metallic surfaces.

questions.question: What causes the force of friction between two solid surfaces?
options: The electrostatic charge built up on the surfaces
The magnetic properties of the materials
The roughness of the surfaces
The gravitational attraction between the surfaces

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of adding a lubricant between two surfaces?
options: To increase the surface area of contact
To reduce friction between the surfaces
To increase the grip between the surfaces
To make the surfaces hotter

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure forces?
options: A thermometer
A newton meter
A measuring cylinder
A balance scale

questions.question: In what unit are forces measured?
options: Kilograms (kg)
Joules (J)
Newtons (N)
Metres per second (m/s)

questions.question: In an experiment, when should you use a bar chart to display your results?
options: When the variable you changed is continuous.
When the variable you changed is categoric.
When you have only measured one data point.
When there are no variables in the experiment.

questions.question: In a fair test, which variables are changed?
options: Only the variable we are testing is changed.
All variables are changed at the same time.
No variables are changed at all.
Only the variables we want to keep the same are changed.

questions.question: How do contact forces act on objects?
options: Only when the objects are touching.
Only when the objects are far apart.
Without the objects needing to touch.
Only in a complete vacuum.

questions.question: How do non-contact forces differ from contact forces?
options: They can only act when objects are directly rubbing against each other.
They can act with or without the objects touching.
They only act when objects are moving at high speeds.
They cannot act across any distance.

questions.question: When drawing a force diagram, what does the length of a force arrow represent?
options: The duration the force is applied for
The size of the force
The speed of the object
The mass of the object

questions.question: Why does an object with a greater mass require a greater force to change its motion?
options: Because objects with greater mass need a greater force to start or stop moving, and to change direction.
Because greater mass automatically reduces the friction acting on it.
Because heavier objects do not experience any gravitational pull.
Because mass decreases as the speed of an object increases.

questions.question: What is the scientific definition of a force?
options: A measure of the amount of matter in an object
A push or a pull
The speed at which an object travels
The energy stored within an object

questions.question: What is needed to change the motion or shape of an object?
options: A force
A lubricant
A bar chart
A change in temperature
